title: A Useless Queen: Recognize the Final Bishop Mate
summary: A queen cannot block an adjacent bishop check: use the king and pawns to account for every escape.

nodes.question: Why can the queen not save this exact position?
nodes.explanation: Bg3 checks Kh4 on an adjacent diagonal. The queen on e2 cannot interpose or capture the bishop, while White’s king and h-pawn seal the exits.

branches.title: Final source pattern after Qe2
commentary: Begin after the source’s Qe2. The queen is on e2 rather than the caption’s a2; all ten pieces remain, including a4 and a5.

Bg3# checks Kh4 on the adjacent diagonal. Kh2 protects g3 and h3, h3 covers g4, and Black’s own g5/h5 pawns occupy the other flights. Qe2 cannot capture g3 or block an adjacent check. Black has no legal reply: actual mate.

exercises.prompt: Why can a queen not interpose here?
exercises.answer: The checking bishop on g3 is next to the king on h4. There is no square between them on which any defender can interpose.

exercises.prompt: Does this prove every Black reply to Bd6 loses?
exercises.answer: No. This exercise verifies the illustrated Qe2/Bg3 mate. The omitted Qg1+ resource and resulting larger ending require separate analysis.

startContext: Final bishop-mate pattern only, after the illustrated Qe2 at121–122 seconds. Native28/29 establish the complete ten-piece diagram: White Kh2/Bd6/a4/g2/h3 against Kh4/Qe2/a5/g5/h5; native30/31 confirm Bg3 mate. The caption says Qa2, but the visible queen is on e2. Bg3# is proved by an exact finite certificate ending in actual mate, with both a4/a5 pawns retained. This does not certify the earlier rook sacrifice, the complete Bd6 waiting plan or every queen defense. In particular, Bd6/Qg1+/Kxg1/g4 reaches a larger ending still needing outcome analysis; that legal resource is preserved in the earlier draft rather than omitted as impossible. A broader bounded strategy search was not used as an exact proof.
